newsitem.title: CHINA: China Development Bank says energy is loan focus.
newsitem.headline: China Development Bank says energy is loan focus.

text.p: China's State Development Bank had extended loans to the nation's energy sector of 81.79 billion yuan ($9.8 billion) by the end of last year, accounting for 48.2 percent of its loan portfolio, bank official Li Baoping said on Tuesday.
Li, director general of the bank's foreign affairs department, said that power development accounted for 51.4 billion yuan of the loans made in 1994 and 1995.
The bank was set up in 1994 to focus on long-term policy lending to support key sectors of the economy.
Li gave no figures for new loans made this year.
The official, who was speaking to an energy conference, also said that in future the bank would focus its lending for oil and natural gas development on China's poorer, inland regions.

China is trying to speed production from its onshore oil and gas fields in the far western region of Xinjiang and elsewhere as part of its drive to slow a sharp rise in energy imports that has accompanied rapid economic development.
It also is trying to reduce the gap in economic development between the inland areas and the fast-growing east coast.
Li said that most loans made by the bank are for projects backed by the State Council, or cabinet.

The bank was formed as part of a move to create a separate policy bank and reduce the number of policy loans made by state-run commercial banks. That was seen as a way to encourage commercial banks to lend funds on market-based decisions and reduce the role of central planning in the banking system.
Despite the reform, China's commercial banking system is often called on to fund ailing state industries that are unable to make repayment.
